title: Market anatomy matrix
description: One market a venture sells into, described on standard dimensions so that what counts as enough evidence can be derived from it rather than fixed (EE-157). Each cell holds a value with its status (known, estimated or unknown, and unknown is never null), its cited evidence graded like any validation evidence, and when it was true (valid_from, valid_to). The calibration in packages/naive/src/engine/gate-calibration.mjs reads it to propose the venture's phase gate thresholds.

segment.description: Who buys, in the venture's words; the ICP it serves when one exists

icp.description: The ideal customer profile id this market is for

primary.description: The market the current phase's gate is calibrated against

industry.description: The industry anatomy id (often a NAICS code) this market sits in

reachable_buyers.description: How many buying organizations or people the venture can actually reach now (serviceable obtainable market as a head count, not dollars)

serviceable_market_usd.description: Serviceable available market per year in US dollars (Blank and Dorf; Steve Blank's TAM, SAM, SOM)

deal_size_usd.description: Expected annual contract value or yearly spend per buyer, in US dollars

sales_cycle_days.description: Days from first conversation to a signed purchase

buying_roles.description: How many roles must agree to a purchase (the buying center, Webster and Wind 1972)

purchase_frequency.description: once, yearly, monthly, weekly or daily

maturity.description: emerging, growth, mature or declining (market life cycle)

concentration.description: fragmented, moderate or concentrated (by HHI bands: under 1500, 1500 to 2500, over 2500)
